english: In a triangle $ABC$, let $a,b,c$ denote the lengths of the sides opposite to the angles $A,B,C$, respectively. The incircle of the triangle and the excircle opposite to the vertex $A$ touch the side $BC$ at the points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. If the inradius is $7$, the radius of the excircle opposite to $A$ is $12$ and $PQ=8$, then the area of the triangle $ABC$ is ______.
hindi: एक त्रिभुज $ABC$ में माना $a,b,c$ क्रमशः कोणों $A,B,C$ की सम्मुख भुजाओं की लम्बाइयाँ हैं। त्रिभुज का अन्तःवृत्त तथा शीर्ष $A$ के सम्मुख बाह्यवृत्त भुजा $BC$ को क्रमशः बिन्दुओं $P$ तथा $Q$ पर स्पर्श करते हैं। यदि अन्तःत्रिज्या $7$ है, शीर्ष $A$ के सम्मुख बाह्यवृत्त की त्रिज्या $12$ है तथा $PQ=8$ है, तो त्रिभुज $ABC$ का क्षेत्रफल ______ है।
solution_full: Let $x=s-b$ and $y=s-c$. The incircle touches $BC$ at $P$ with $BP=s-b=x$; the excircle opposite to $A$ touches $BC$ at $Q$ with $BQ=s-c=y$.
Check: $b=s-x$, $c=s-y$ are $42,34$ (in some order); Heron: $\sqrt{48\cdot28\cdot6\cdot14}=\sqrt{112896}=336$, and $\dfrac{336}{28}=12=r_1$.
originality_note: New: the two points where the incircle and the A-excircle touch BC are given by their distance, which equals |b - c|, and together with r r1 = (s-b)(s-c) this fixes s - b and s - c (way 5: excircle and incircle tangent lengths combined with the product of radii). Closest known: 'given r1, r2, r3 find the area' (1/r = sum 1/r_i, Delta^2 = r r1 r2 r3). Different because: only r and r1 are given, and the missing datum is a distance on BC that must be read as b - c.
stem_review: Read as a student: every point, side, angle and symbol is introduced before use, all conditions are stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that the data give a real triangle (20, 42, 34) and that the order of b and c does not change the area. Changed: No change.
key_step: Reading PQ as |b - c| and using r r1 = (s-b)(s-c) to get s - b and s - c.
justification: Routine chain of standard incircle/excircle results with one small link (PQ = |b - c|); numerical but no casework. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q18 (L2), below the inradius part 2023-P2-Q15 (L4).

concept_use.Excenters and exradius: BQ = s - c for the A-excircle and r1 = Delta/(s-a), giving r1/r = s/(s-a).
concept_use.Inradius and incenter based questions: BP = s - b for the incircle, r = Delta/s, and r r1 = (s-b)(s-c).
